source_text: Igitur postquam sibi unum de praefatiuncola prioris operis mei caput, quod quasi impugnaret, obiecit illudque de figulo peccatorum Deo suo subdidit, me arguit; quam sane constanter et pure ipsius eloquiis publicetur: Non itaque, sicut te atque alios fallens loqueris, si quis aut liberum in hominibus arbitrium aut Deum esse nascentium conditorem dixerit, Caelestianus et Pelagianus vocatur, ista quippe et catholica fides dicit. Sed si quis ad colendum recte Deum sine ipsius adiutorio dicit esse in hominibus liberum arbitrium et quisquis ita dicit Deum nascentium conditorem, ut parvulorum neget a potestate diaboli redemptorem, ipse Caelestianus et Pelagianus vocatur. Liberum itaque arbitrium esse in hominibus et Deum esse nascentium conditorem utrique dicimus; non hinc estis Caelestiani et Pelagiani. Liberum autem esse quemquam ad agendum bonum sine adiutorio Dei et non erui parvulos a potestate tenebrarum, et sic transferri in regnum Dei [n126] hoc vos dicitis; hinc estis Caelestiani et Pelagiani [n127] . Natare te quidem in impietatis tuae et formidinis palude frequenter ostendi nec super hoc dubitaturum prudentem constat esse lectorem.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore after he objected to himself one head from the little preface of my prior work, which he might as it were impugn, and subjected that about the potter of sinners to his god, he argues me; let it be publicized how constantly and purely by his own elocutions: It is not therefore, as you speak deceiving yourself and others, if anyone has said either that there is free choice in humans or that God is the founder of those being born, he is called Caelestian and Pelagian, for the catholic faith also says these. But if anyone says that there is in humans free choice for worshiping God rightly without his help, and whoever so says God is the founder of those being born that he denies the redeemer of little ones from the power of the devil, he himself is called Caelestian and Pelagian. We both therefore say that there is free choice in humans and that God is the founder of those being born; not from here are you Caelestians and Pelagians. But that anyone is free for doing good without the help of God and that little ones are not plucked from the power of darkness and thus transferred into the kingdom of God—this you say; from here you are Caelestians and Pelagians. That you swim in the swamp of your impiety and fear I have frequently shown, and it stands that a prudent reader will not doubt over this.

pass_b_english: After putting forward one passage from the brief preface of my earlier work as though to attack it, and adding his claim about his god as the potter of sinners, he accuses me. Let his own words display how consistent and straightforward he is:

‘It is not, then, as you say while deceiving yourself and others, that anyone who says humans have free will or that God creates newborn children is called a Caelestian and Pelagian. The catholic faith says these things too. But anyone who says humans have free will to worship God rightly without God’s help, and anyone who calls God the creator of newborn children in such a way as to deny that he redeems infants from the devil’s power, is called a Caelestian and Pelagian. Both of us, therefore, say that humans have free will and God is the creator of newborn children. That is not why you are Caelestians and Pelagians. But that anyone is free to do good without God’s help, and that infants are not rescued from the power of darkness and thus transferred into God’s kingdom—these are your claims. That is why you are Caelestians and Pelagians’ (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.8; compare Colossians 1:13).
I have frequently shown you floundering in the swamp of your irreverence and fear; a sensible reader surely will not doubt it.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
